scope: Brief summaries of public site descriptions; source holdout analyses not rerun, site heads may change, and current artifacts differ from the pinned historical files.

GEMSDOE24.current_review: The site describes S3DEP1, a terrain-based 10 m elevation research file, as its point-best local holdout. It also reports literal registry failure and unresolved mimics including highway cut and fill. Its scientific measurements were not replayed here.
GEMSDOE24.historical_review: The 60,069-dot H19-5 re-thinned file is in the same closely overlapping family as the eight comparators. Its unverified claimed result is not a current-candidate score.

GEMSDOE25.current_review: The H79-CTHM work combines subsurface and thermo-mechanical indicators with an SGMC-derived signal. The site reports that its research file trails its stronger H35 control and fails the literal lattice gate, even though it passes a narrower sparse-raster screen. We did not replay the holdout.
GEMSDOE25.historical_review: The pinned D2.8 file has exactly the same positive support as the pinned GEMSDOE30 archive, despite different TIFF bytes. Their claimed score-to-file receipts remain unavailable.

GEMSDOE27.current_review: A buried-step complement research raster is described as below its base control, with a uniqueness check limited to a subset of references and an unmatched current-best control. The site's own disposition is negative; we did not rerun the experiment.
GEMSDOE27.historical_review: The pinned topo-gap-closure archive is a denser, 61,328-dot historical member and exceeds the proximity threshold against every other named historical reference.

GEMSDOE28.current_review: The site's S23 audit withdraws an inherited approval and reports a literal lattice conflict; a previously cited S22C holdout lacked the requested buffer. The nine-site forensic audit informed this independent byte-level reproduction.
GEMSDOE28.historical_review: The pinned rung30 historical map has 37,660 positive footprint pixels and exceeds the proximity threshold against each of the other eight historical maps.

GEMSDOE30.current_review: The source reports that a pooled multi-feature POOL-1 lane beat its matched holdout control, but its output failed the literal dot-overlap gate against multiple registered files; it did not publish a TIFF. Results were not replayed here and do not establish a live score.
GEMSDOE30.historical_review: The pinned 44,090-dot Poisson-spaced archive has identical positive support to the pinned GEMSDOE25 archive. A larger dot budget worsens the lattice counting obstruction.

GEMSDOE31.current_review: The H31-AA research lane uses piedmont log-flexure and a paleoshoreline-null idea. The site reports that its chosen arm fell below its same-run incumbent, while its release review also identifies a lattice stop. Source holdouts were not replayed here.
GEMSDOE31.historical_review: The pinned historical 40,199-dot support contains every GEMSDOE32 H33-B2 dot, with 2,545 additional dots; this is a support relationship, not evidence of score causation.

GEMSDOE32.current_review: The H48 research file is described as improving a same-protocol hide-recover comparison but underperforming the H33 reference on an off-catalogue proxy and failing literal lattice overlap. The site does not authorize upload. Neither holdout was replayed here.
GEMSDOE32.historical_review: H33-B2 is exactly the GEMSDOE25 historical support after removing points within two pixels of the mirrored catalogue. The owner-reported 0.2778 lacks a file-bound organizer receipt; its mechanism is not established.

GEMSDOE33.current_review: The A33-R5 radiometric Th/K, conductivity and shallow-cover research method failed its stated holdout gates. Its reported novelty covers 21 references, not proof against the full literal registry. We did not replay the source holdout.
GEMSDOE33.historical_review: The 41,865-dot tip/stepover archive overlaps the other named historical files beyond the stop threshold. Its claimed result is not a calibrated forecast for later methods.

GEMSDOE36.current_review: The TCD-36 terrain and fluvial-chi method is described as improving its local holdout control, but its published dot map exceeds literal lattice overlap and is not cleared. We did not replay the result or infer a private score.
GEMSDOE36.historical_review: The pinned 38,854-dot historical support includes the H33-B2 support plus 1,200 dots. It is not a distinct competition candidate under the directed proximity rule.
